# Oxford English Dictionary

> > The definitive historical dictionary of the English language, documenting etymology, pronunciation, definitions, and usage of words from Old English to modern times.

The Oxford English Dictionary (OED) is the authoritative scholarly resource for English language lexicography, tracing word origins through Latin, French, Middle English, and other source languages. Each entry provides comprehensive etymological analysis, historical quotations, pronunciation guides, and frequency data for words ranging from common usage to obsolete and rare terms.

## Key Topics

- etymology
- historical linguistics
- lexicography
- Latin borrowings
- Middle English
- word definitions
- pronunciation guides
- word frequency
- historical usage
- obsolete words
- Old English
- French loanwords
- dictionary entries
- word history

- [abidance, n.](https://www.oed.com/dictionary/abidance_n): Etymology, pronunciation, and historical usage
- [abetter, n.](https://www.oed.com/dictionary/abetter_n): Middle English noun with etymology and frequency
- [Abbasid, n. & adj.](https://www.oed.com/dictionary/abbasid_n): Noun/adjective with Latin etymology and frequency
- [abdominous, adj.](https://www.oed.com/dictionary/abdominous_adj): 17th-century Latin borrowing adjective
- [abdicable, adj.](https://www.oed.com/dictionary/abdicable_adj): Latin borrowing adjective with etymology
- [abductive, adj.](https://www.oed.com/dictionary/abductive_adj): Adjective with etymology and frequency data
- [abas, n.](https://www.oed.com/dictionary/abas_n): French loanword noun with historical usage
- [abjurement, n.](https://www.oed.com/dictionary/abjurement_n): Noun with historical usage by Michael Drayton
- [aberration, n.](https://www.oed.com/dictionary/aberration_n): Etymology, pronunciation, and frequency data
- [abi, adv.](https://www.oed.com/dictionary/abi_adv): Nigerian English adverb from Yoruba language
- [abhorrently, adv.](https://www.oed.com/dictionary/abhorrently_adv): Adverb with etymology and frequency guide

## Specialized and Technical Terms

- [A and E](https://www.oed.com/dictionary/a-and-e_x): British medical abbreviation for Accident & Emergency
- [ab intestato, adv.](https://www.oed.com/dictionary/ab-intestato_adv): Latin legal term for intestate succession
- [ablaqueate, v.](https://www.oed.com/dictionary/ablaqueate_v): Latin borrowing verb from Middle English
- [abbozzo, n.](https://www.oed.com/dictionary/abbozzo_n): Rare Italian loanword in art/literary terminology

## Obsolete and Historical Words

- [ablactate, v.](https://www.oed.com/dictionary/ablactate_v): Obsolete 1700s Latin-derived verb
- [abietite, n.](https://www.oed.com/dictionary/abietite_n): Obsolete 1860s German chemical term
- [abbatie, n.](https://www.oed.com/dictionary/abbatie_n): Obsolete Middle English noun from French/Latin
- [abbotess, n.](https://www.oed.com/dictionary/abbotess_n): Obsolete Old English noun from Latin
- [abjudication, n.](https://www.oed.com/dictionary/abjudication_n): Archaic Latin-derived noun from 1600s
